name: Allam-Fetvedt cycle (oxy-combustion supercritical CO2 power)
applications: natural gas power with inherent capture

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Natural gas burns in oxygen diluted with hot recycled CO2. The high-pressure CO2 and water mixture drives a turbine, is cooled in a recuperator, and the water is condensed out. Most CO2 is recompressed and recycled; the excess is near-pure and goes straight to a pipeline.

advantages: Capture is inherent to the cycle; no separate capture plant
Pipeline-ready CO2

name: Amine solvent post-combustion capture

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Flue gas is cooled and contacted counter-currently with an aqueous amine solution, which reacts with CO2. The CO2-rich solution is heated with low-pressure steam in a stripper, releasing a near-pure CO2 stream and regenerating the solvent for reuse. Vendors differ mainly in solvent formulation, heat integration and solvent management.

name: Bioenergy with CCS (BECCS)
aliases: bioenergy with carbon capture and storage

name: Calcium looping
applications: cement (purge CaO usable as raw meal)

source.note: Energy & Fuels 38(15), 2024, CC BY 4.0: pilot at TRL7; IEAGHG 2019 gave TRL 6

principle: Lime (CaO) captures CO2 from flue gas in a carbonator at about 650 °C, forming CaCO3. The solids circulate to a calciner at about 900-950 °C, fired with fuel in oxygen and CO2, which releases a concentrated CO2 stream and regenerates CaO. Fresh limestone is added to make up for sorbent decay.

process_steps.name: Heat recovery, CO2 purification and compression

key_equipment: two interconnected circulating fluidised bed reactors

reference_plants.capacity: 1.7 MWth

advantages: Cheap, abundant sorbent (limestone)
High-temperature heat can be recovered for power
Synergy with cement: spent CaO is a raw material
limitations: Needs an air separation unit for the calciner
Sorbent activity decays with cycles, so make-up and purge are needed

name: Chemical looping combustion

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: A solid metal oxide oxygen carrier circulates between an air reactor, where it picks up oxygen, and a fuel reactor, where it burns the fuel without contact with air. The fuel reactor exhaust is only CO2 and water, so CO2 is obtained by condensing the water, without an air separation unit.

suppliers.name: Research stage; no commercial licensor identified in the cited sources

advantages: Inherent CO2 separation with no air separation unit
limitations: Oxygen carrier attrition and lifetime
Solids circulation at scale not yet demonstrated commercially

name: CO2 mineralisation (in-situ basalt)
principle: CO2 is dissolved in water at the surface and injected into basalt, where it reacts with calcium, magnesium and iron in the rock to form carbonate minerals. IEA rates CO2 mineralisation (inert carbonate materials) at TRL 9.

name: Physical solvent acid gas removal (pre-combustion)

The rich solvent is depressurised in stages to release CO2, then stripped, and returned to the absorber. Physical solvents favour high-pressure syngas, while chemical solvents suit low partial pressures.

limitations: Needs high pressure and high CO2 partial pressure

name: Geological CO2 storage in saline aquifers
applications: permanent storage of captured CO2 from industry, power and gas processing
principle: Captured CO2 is compressed to a dense phase, piped or shipped to an injection site and injected through wells into a porous rock formation filled with salt water, below an impermeable caprock. The CO2 is trapped under the seal, dissolves in the brine and, over long periods, can mineralise. Injection raises reservoir pressure, so capacity is limited by the pressure that the rock and caprock can tolerate; operators manage it with well placement, completion design and sometimes brine production. Monitoring wells and surveys track the plume.

performance.metric: storage capacity gain from lateral pressure redistribution by brine production, Natuna D-Alpha (simulation)
performance.basis: thick carbonate aquifer; high-rate brine production; multi-depth injection alone gave 13%, both together 44% with storage efficiency 0.58%

source.note: Nirwana et al., Optimizing CO2 Storage in Saline Aquifers through Pressure Redistribution in Natuna D-Alpha Field, SCOG 49(3): 53-66, 2026 (LEMIGAS SCOG, CC BY-SA 4.0)

performance.metric: increase in stored CO2 from completion redesign, SK gas field aquifer (simulation)
performance.basis: 120-year simulation with plume confined to the aquifer zone in most cases; mineral trapping a minor share

source.note: Iskandar et al., Optimized CO2 storage strategies for plume containment and mineral trapping in the SK gas field aquifer, SCOG 49(2): 173-201, 2026 (LEMIGAS SCOG, CC BY-SA 4.0)

performance.metric: pore pressure rise and remaining margin to fracture pressure, sandstone at 1,200 m (simulation)

name: Blast-resistant buildings
principle: Occupied buildings inside blast overpressure range are engineered to protect people, not just stand up: energy-absorbing steel or reinforced concrete construction, controlled response (ductile, repairable deformation rather than brittle failure), protected openings, and anchored doors and HVAC. Design starts from a siting study and quantified overpressure/impulse from dispersion and explosion modelling (API RP 752/753 onshore; temporary refuge criteria offshore), then verifies member response against that loading.

Building designed for the design blast with acceptable response limits
Module or building fabricated and certified
Occupancy controls keep people outside the blast zone where possible

name: Structural fireproofing and passive fire protection
principle: Passive fire protection keeps steel below its critical temperature and confines fire by barriers without any active system: cementitious and epoxy intumescent coatings on structure, fire-rated walls, doors and dampers, deck insulation offshore, and fire-protected cabling or trays. Protection classes follow hydrocarbon fire curves (UL 1709 rather than cellulosic) for process zones; the design allocates fireproofing from fire modelling and layout (API 2218 guidance), and inspection regimes track coating condition because PFP failure is invisible until it is needed.

process_steps.name: Fire protection mapping allocates ratings from layout and fire scenarios
Coating or barrier system selected for the fire curve and duration
Applied on primed, pre-insulated or live-duty steel per system data sheet
Inspection and repair regime tracks adhesion and thickness

performance.metric: intumescent coating thickness for a 90-minute rating
performance.basis: 1.50 mm DFT (about 2.6 kg/m2) gives 90 minutes at Hp/A 150.

coating damage from mechanical impact is common and often repaired poorly
advantages: no activation, no power, no maintenance loop — protection is built in
preserves evacuation time and structural integrity in the first critical minutes

name: FPSO and floating production structures
principle: Floating production systems keep process plant on a floating hull: converted tankers or newbuild FPSOs, semi-submersibles or spar hulls, held by moorings or dynamic positioning. Hull design, station-keeping, riser and umbilical dynamics, and motion effects on process equipment (sloshing, level control, rotating equipment limits) define the engineering.

name: Foundations and piling
principle: Foundations transfer structural loads to the ground safely and within settlement limits. Shallow footings serve competent soils; driven or bored piles take loads past weak layers; ground improvement (stone columns, deep soil mixing, preloading) treats marginal ground instead of deep foundations. Site investigation drives everything — boreholes, SPT/CPT profiles, groundwater — and equipment foundations add dynamic checks for machines, plus settlement and vibration limits.

process_steps.name: Geotechnical investigation characterises strata and groundwater
Foundation type chosen: shallow, deep or ground improvement
Piles driven or bored, footings cast, ground improved
Load or integrity tests verify capacity

advantages: mature, testable technology with local contractors nearly everywhere
ground improvement often beats deep foundations on cost for marginal soils

name: Heavy lift, transport and temporary works
principle: Heavy lift and transport engineering plans how very large loads are lifted, rolled or floated into position: engineered rigging, crane or gantry selection, ground bearing assessments, SPMT trailer configurations, transport surveys and lifts supervised by independent checking engineers. Temporary works — cradle supports, lifting frames, hauling systems, shoring — are designed, certified and inspected like permanent structures. Success is almost entirely preparation: surveys, simulations and rehearsals before the load moves.

Lift plan: crane or gantry, rigging, load path and contingency
Temporary works designed, certified and inspected

advantages: makes factory-built modules practical at multi-thousand-tonne scale
shutdown durations shrink when big items lift out and in as one piece

name: Modular construction and industrialised building systems
principle: Modular construction moves fabrication from the congested site into controlled workshops: equipment, piping, cable and steel are assembled into transportable modules (skids, multi-storey modules, e-houses), shipped, lifted and connected on site. Benefits are schedule compression, quality, weather independence, lower site headcount and local content limits; the trade-offs are transport envelope limits, module weight for lifting, joint design at every module interface, and early engineering freeze. Industrialised Building Systems (IBS) applies the same offsite logic to buildings — precast components, panelised and volumetric systems — promoted in Malaysia through the CIDB IBS programme with content and scoring rules.

process_steps.name: Facility split into modules within transport and lift limits
Modules fabricated, piped, cabled and inspected in the yard
Modules transported by road, barge or vessel
Modules set, levelled and interconnects (piping, cable, tie-ins) completed

performance.basis: IBS projects save up to 30% of construction time; CIDB case studies show near cost parity.

source.note: Mydin, E3S Web of Conferences (2014), read 2026-11-17

limitations: module interfaces concentrate risk: every split is a fabricated joint on site
early freeze conflicts with normal design iteration; the schedule benefit is lost if design is late
advantages: yard quality and productivity transfer to site as compressed schedule and lower headcount
e-houses and skids reduce hot work and congested-site labour exposure

name: Fixed platform topsides and substructures
applications: shallow and medium water fixed platforms
principle: Fixed offshore platforms combine a substructure (welded steel jacket, or concrete gravity-base structure) founded on or pinned to the seabed with a topsides deck carrying drilling, production and power. Jackets are launched or lifted in place and piled through legs; topsides are built as integrated or modularised decks and set by float-over or lift. Design is governed by ISO 19902 (steel) and structural reliability against extreme wave, wind and fatigue loads; weight control and deck elevation against air gap are the persistent constraints.

name: Pipe racks, sleepers and pipe supports
principle: Pipe racks carry interconnecting piping in tiers along roads and unit boundaries; individual supports (shoes, guides, anchors, spring and constant-effort hangers) carry the pipe's own loads while allowing thermal movement. Rack design ties together pipe stress needs (support spacing, guide positions), civil loads (wind, seismic, friction), and constructability (splice points, tier heights). Expansion loops, guides and anchors are positioned from stress analysis, not civil preference.

name: Seismic design of process facilities
principle: In seismic regions, structures, equipment, piping and their connections are designed for earthquake demands: site-specific hazard analysis, response spectrum or time-history analysis, anchorage and support design for equipment, and settlement or fault-movement checks for tanks and pipelines. Codes (ASCE 7, EN 1998, and industry guides such as ASCE 4 and API 650 Appendix E) tier the objectives — keep safety systems functional, prevent release of hazardous inventory, allow economic damage elsewhere. Performance-based methods and base isolation are used where downtime cost dominates.

name: Plant structural steel design
principle: Process plants are steel frames carrying piping, equipment, platforms and loads under gravity, wind, thermal, seismic and blast demands. Designers size members and connections to structural steel codes (EN 1993, AISC 360, ISO 19902 offshore) with deflection and vibration limits that matter as much as strength: pipe rack spans, equipment nozzle flexibility and platform vibration all drive the geometry. Hot-rolled sections dominate onshore; plate girders, tubulars and cast nodes dominate offshore.

process_steps.name: Loads gathered: dead, live, piping, wind, seismic, thermal, blast
Arrangement set: bays, bracing, support locations aligned with piping and access
Members and connections designed to code with serviceability checks
Detailing, galvanising/painting, and connection design for fabrication

performance.basis: AISC case-study building: 400 t with 7 workers in 38 days (1.5 t/worker-day); Empire State reached 1.68 t/worker-day, with low-rise frames at 50-60 kg/m2.

source.note: Construction Physics citing an AISC case study, read 2026-11-17

limitations: late piping changes propagate into steel redesign — freezing steelwork late is the classic schedule risk
thermal expansion of headers needs sliding supports and guides that survive both hot and cold cases
advantages: standardised, fabricable, demountable framing suits modular construction
steel density keeps topsides weight — the offshore design currency — under control

name: Computerised maintenance management and work management
principle: The CMMS (or enterprise asset management system) is the operational record of every physical asset: equipment hierarchy, failure history, work orders, permits and spare-parts stock. Work management turns that record into a pipeline — backlog prioritised by risk, planned jobs kitted with materials, scheduled into windows that respect process constraints, executed with capture of as-found/as-left condition, then reviewed in bad-actor and reliability analyses that feed back into inspection and strategy decisions. Its value depends entirely on data discipline: a CMMS full of duplicate hierarchies and un-closed work orders drives worse decisions than paper.

process_steps.name: Asset register and hierarchy maintained from engineering data
Work requests screened, prioritised and planned with materials
Jobs scheduled into windows agreed with operations
Failure and cost history analysed; strategies updated

principle: Cable systems move power and signals between equipment and boards. name: Earthing and lightning protection
applications: tank farm and flare stack protection
principle: Earthing connects metalwork and neutral points to earth so that fault current, lightning and static charge have a safe, low-impedance path and touch voltages stay within limits; lightning protection intercepts strikes with air terminals and down conductors and disposes of the surge through the earth grid. Plant design separates power, instrument and clean earths, bonds across structures and pipelines, and fits surge protective devices on vulnerable circuits. Design rules come from IEC 62305 (lightning), IEC 60364 (installations) and company earth-grid studies for soil resistivity and fault current.

process_steps.name: Soil resistivity surveyed; earth grid sized for fault current and step/touch limits
Metalwork, structures and cable armour bonded into the grid
Air terminals, down conductors and earth termination intercept and discharge strikes
Surge protective devices staged on power and signal circuits

performance.basis: TNB transmission at 132-500 kV drives arresters and clearances

limitations: corrosive soils and cathodic protection interactions need deliberate earthing material choices
verification is periodic and physical: resistance and continuity testing across the grid
advantages: the single cheapest safeguard against electric shock, fire and lightning damage
instrument earthing discipline protects low-level signals from circulating currents

name: Emergency, standby and UPS power systems
principle: A facility secures loads that must not fail through layers: battery-backed uninterruptible power supplies (classified VFI, VI or DXI by output dependency under IEC 62040-3) ride through the first seconds, standby generating sets start and close onto the emergency bus, and automatic transfer switching restores normal supply after the outage. name: On-site gas turbine power generation
applications: island and parallel operation with the grid
principle: Facilities generate their own power with gas turbine generator sets when the grid is weak, absent or considered unreliable, or when waste heat from exhaust can drive steam for process use (cogeneration). name: Hazardous area electrical equipment
principle: Where flammable atmospheres can occur, electrical equipment is selected to exclude or contain ignition sources. Areas are classified by likelihood and duration (gas: Zone 0/1/2; dust: Zone 20/21/22) under IEC 60079-10 or DSEAR in the UK, then protected by equipment protection concepts matched to the zone: intrinsic safety (Ex ia/ib) for instrumentation, flameproof enclosures (Ex d), increased safety (Ex e), pressurisation (Ex p), encapsulation (Ex m) and others. The IECEx certification system covers equipment certification, conformity of installation and personnel competence across member countries.

process_steps.name: Hazardous area classification maps zones from leak sources and dispersion
Ex protection concept selected per zone and equipment group
Certified installation with correct glands, bonding and segregation
Initial and periodic inspections verify Ex integrity

name: Electrical heat tracing
principle: Electrical heat tracing maintains or raises the temperature of pipes, tanks and instruments by applying heat along the surface. Self-regulating parallel trace cables vary their resistance with temperature and cannot overheat a dry section, constant-wattage cables deliver fixed power, and mineral-insulated or skin-effect systems serve long, hot or high-power duties. Heating replaces or supplements steam tracing, and digital control panels monitor every circuit for current and temperature alarms.

name: HV/MV switchgear and site power distribution
principle: Medium-voltage switchgear receives, protects and distributes electrical power across a facility. Power arrives from utility infeed or site generation at high voltage (typically 132 kV and above for large plants), is transformed to a main distribution voltage (usually 11 kV or 33/36 kV onshore, 11 kV offshore), and flows through switchboards to transformers, motors and downstream boards. Air-insulated, gas-insulated (GIS) and hybrid designs exist; modern breakers use vacuum or SF6 interrupting technology.

Distribution transformers step down to LV or lower MV levels
Motor control centres and LV boards feed process loads
Downstream faults are cleared selectively by graded protection

name: Motors and variable speed drives
principle: Three-phase induction motors remain the workhorse driver; synchronous machines serve large compressors and high-efficiency duties. Efficiency classes IE1 to IE5 are defined in IEC 60034-30-1 for line-operated motors. Variable frequency drives rectify the supply and synthesise an adjustable-voltage, adjustable-frequency output, giving soft starts, process speed control, energy savings on centrifugal loads (affinity laws: power roughly follows speed cubed) and regenerative braking on hoisting duties. Drives inject harmonics, so input filters or multi-pulse/active front ends are applied.

name: Power management and electrical SCADA
principle: A power management system supervises generation, tie-lines and major loads: it schedules and dispatches running generator sets, synchronises and parallels them, maintains frequency and voltage, arms staged load shedding for generator or tie loss, and manages islanding and re-synchronisation with the grid. PMS logic sits on electrical SCADA above the protection relays and complements them — protection clears faults in milliseconds while the PMS re-balances the network in seconds.

Generation dispatched and synchronised against demand and reserve targets
Staged load shedding armed and executed on disturbance
Islanding, closed-bus transfer and re-sync managed

name: Power system protection and relaying
principle: Protection relays continuously compare measured current, voltage, frequency, phase and differential quantities against settings and command circuit breakers to isolate faults before equipment or people are harmed. Modern numerical relays combine many protection functions (ANSI 50/51 overcurrent, 87 differential, 27/59 voltage, 81 frequency, 46 negative sequence) with recording, metering and IEC 61850 communication in one device. Selectivity is achieved through current grading, time grading or zone-based differential schemes, with breaker-failure back-up tripping the surrounding breakers when the primary trip fails.

process_steps.name: Current and voltage transformers scale primary quantities to relay inputs
Relays compute protection elements and compare with settings
Grading and zone logic discriminate in-zone faults from load
Trip output opens the correct breaker(s); breaker-failure back-up trips wider if needed
Event and disturbance records support post-fault analysis

name: Subsea power and umbilical systems
principle: Subsea electrical systems take power from a platform or shore through a power umbilical — cable plus steel tubes for hydraulic signals — to subsea distribution units, transformers, variable speed drives and motors on the seabed. Moves toward higher voltage and longer step-outs have already delivered megawatt-class subsea compression, where the whole drive train sits on the seabed without an topsides compressor. Reliability engineering, connector technology and dynamic cable design for floating hosts dominate the design space.

Power umbilical and static/dynamic cable delivered to the seabed
Subsea distribution and step-down feed seabed loads
Motors, drives and valve actuators run on the seabed

dynamic cables on floating production see fatigue that dominates their design
advantages: eliminates long risers and topsides compression weight and space
enables long-distance tiebacks and seabed boosting where topsides power would be prohibitive

name: Power and distribution transformers
principle: Transformers couple windings through a magnetic core to change voltage levels at essentially constant power. Oil-filled units (mineral oil, ester or gas-insulated) dominate power ratings, with ONAN/ONAF/OFAF/ODAF cooling stages; dry-type cast-resin units suit fire-sensitive or confined locations. An on-load tap changer (OLTC) regulates the output voltage under load. Losses, sound level and thermal behaviour are standardised in the IEC 60076 series.

name: Boil-off gas management and reliquefaction

name: Molecular sieve and glycol dehydration
applications: LNG and NGL cryogenic plants (molecular sieve)
principle: Water is removed so it cannot form hydrates, ice or corrosive liquids. Glycol units absorb water into triethylene glycol, which is regenerated by heating, and are enough for pipeline specifications. Cryogenic plants use molecular sieve beds that adsorb water to very low levels and are regenerated by hot gas in a timed cycle. NETL's LNG model dries gas to below 0.5 ppmv water ahead of liquefaction.

performance.metric: water content after molecular sieve dehydration for LNG
performance.basis: NETL LNG pretreatment assumption (below 0.5 ppmv)

source.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B

advantages: Mature and simple
Molecular sieves reach cryogenic dryness
Glycol units are low cost for pipeline gas
limitations: Glycol regeneration vents BTEX and methane unless controlled
Molecular sieves need regeneration heat and periodic replacement
Adsorbent dusting can foul downstream exchangers

name: Liquid redox sulfur recovery (LO-CAT)
principle: Hydrogen sulfide is absorbed into an aqueous solution of an iron chelate catalyst, where it is oxidised to elemental sulfur (H2S + 1/2 O2 -> S + H2O). The reduced catalyst is regenerated by air in an oxidiser, and the sulfur is separated as a slurry or cake. The process suits small to mid-size H2S loads and streams that are too lean or too dilute for a Claus plant.

name: Membrane CO2 removal for high-CO2 gas
applications: bulk CO2 removal ahead of amines
principle: Gas flows past a polymer membrane. CO2, H2S and water dissolve into and diffuse through the polymer faster than methane, so they collect on the low-pressure permeate side while methane stays at pressure in the residue. Pretreatment protects the membrane from liquids and heavy hydrocarbons, and two stages or a permeate compressor can be used to reduce methane losses.

name: Mercury removal units
applications: gas processing with aluminium cryogenic exchangers
principle: Gas passes through fixed beds of sorbent, typically metal sulfides on alumina, which react irreversibly with mercury to form stable mercury sulfide. Mercury must be removed because it corrodes aluminium cryogenic heat exchangers. Modern designs place the beds upstream, close to the wells, rather than downstream of dryers as was common historically.

Upstream placement limits contamination of the whole plant
limitations: Spent sorbent is hazardous waste
Upstream beds must tolerate wet, high-pressure gas
Mercury can also be carried into liquids and needs separate treatment

name: Physical solvent gas treating (Selexol, Rectisol, Purisol)
applications: separate H2S and CO2 streams for sulfur recovery and CO2 storage or EOR
principle: Acid gases dissolve in an organic solvent in proportion to their partial pressure, with no chemical reaction. The rich solvent is released by pressure letdown, flashing and, where H2S must be sent to sulfur recovery, heat or stripping gas, so regeneration needs less heat than amine. Selexol uses dimethyl ethers of polyethylene glycol; Rectisol uses refrigerated methanol. Because capacity rises with pressure, physical solvents suit high-pressure gas such as gasification syngas and not low-pressure gas.

process_steps.name: Feed gas cooling and water removal
Acid gas absorption at high pressure
Staged flash of rich solvent (CO2 release, recycle of co-absorbed hydrocarbons)

name: Turbo-expander NGL recovery (GSP, RSV processes)
principle: Dry gas is chilled against cold residue gas, then expanded through a turbo-expander, which cools it further and drives a recompressor. Ortloff variants such as GSP and RSV use subcooled reflux or recycled residue gas to raise ethane recovery, and can switch to ethane rejection while keeping propane recovery high.

name: Biogas upgrading to biomethane
principle: Licensor-first flow (DMT/Pentair published trains): raw biogas (~60% CH4, ~1% H2S) is compressed, H2S removed biologically or on carbon, then CO2 separated by water wash, amine wash, membrane separation or PSA to 95-99% methane (grid/vehicle spec); dewpointing and odorisation complete the product. Used at WWTP digesters and farm/landfill biogas alike.

process_steps.name: CO2 separation
equipment: water wash, amine wash, membranes or PSA

performance.basis: amine 0.04 to 0.1% (lowest); membrane 0.5 to 1%; water scrubber 1 to 2%; PSA below 2%; physical adsorption 2 to 4%; cryogenic about 2%

source.note: IEA Bioenergy Task 37, Methane slip from biogas upgrading (January 2023)

performance.metric: biogas upgrading energy use by technology

SGC report: PSA electricity 0.15-0.3 kWh/Nm3; Wantz et al. 2023: high-pressure water scrubber measured 0.8 kWh/Nm3, reducible to 0.3; Khan et al. 2021 review (OSTI): amine regeneration adds 0.1-0.15 kWh/Nm3

name: PEM electrolysis
principle: A solid polymer membrane carries protons from anode to cathode. Water is split at an iridium-based anode into oxygen, protons and electrons; protons cross the membrane and combine with electrons at a platinum-based cathode to form hydrogen. DOE gives 70 to 90 °C operation. The compact cell runs at high current density and follows load quickly.

name: Flare management and gas recovery
principle: The flare is the plant's last line of pressure protection — but routine flaring is now an emissions and cost target. name: AI-training and inference load profiles
applications: Capacity planning and utility interconnection requests for AI campuses

name: Free cooling and economisers

name: Data centre grid interaction (demand response and frequency services)
aliases: Data centre demand response and flexible load
applications: frequency containment and dynamic containment schemes

name: Immersion cooling
applications: Very high density racks where cold plates are insufficient

principle: Immersion cooling puts the server, or a sealed chassis, into a dielectric bath, so heat leaves by direct contact with liquid instead of air. Single-phase systems circulate the fluid to an external heat exchanger; two-phase systems let the fluid boil and condense on a coil. Because the whole board is wetted, density is limited by the tank and fluid rather than by a cold plate's coverage, but service procedures and fluid compatibility change completely.

Point gas detectors (catalytic, infrared, electrochemical), open-path infrared lines, ultrasonic gas leak detectors for high-pressure releases, flame detectors (UV/IR, multispectral), and smoke or heat detection in buildings are placed from coverage mapping rather than guesswork — modern practice models 3D coverage of each head against leak scenarios. The F&G system is usually SIL-rated and integrated with, but independent from, the process SIS.

process_steps.name: Detectors sense gas, flame, smoke or heat
Voting logic confirms the hazard (2oo3, 2ooN) to reject spurious trips
Executive actions started: alarm, deluge, ESD, ventilation
Detector coverage mapped and optimised against leak scenarios

limitations: detector placement is scenario-dependent; a detector that meets a spacing rule may still miss the release that matters
poisoning, fouling and dirty optics degrade gas and flame detectors silently without a test regime
advantages: the first automated response to a leak — seconds matter before escalation
3D coverage mapping turns detector layout from folklore into evidence

name: Turbomachinery control systems
principle: Turbomachinery controllers run the fast, dedicated loops that protect and optimise machines: speed and load control on turbines, surge avoidance on compressors (recycle valves and setpoint margins sized from the compressor map), load sharing between machines, and sequence control for start-up and shutdown. The control system responds in tens of milliseconds — faster than the DCS loop layer — and coordinates with the SIS on trip circuits. Integrated machinery packages ship with controllers tuned to the OEM's model, and online performance monitoring feeds optimisation.

process_steps.name: Speed, load or process demand tracked by fast control loops
Surge control holds operating point off the compressor surge line
Load sharing and sequencing across parallel machines
Start-up, shutdown and purge sequences executed

advantages: prevents surge events that mechanically destroy compressors in seconds
dedicated fast hardware keeps control deterministic where DCS loops cannot

name: Machinery vibration monitoring
principle: Vibration monitoring watches rotating machinery health with proximity probes (shaft displacement on fluid-film bearings), velocity and acceleration sensors (bearing housing), and keyphasor references for phase. Protection systems alarm and trip on vibration limits while continuous condition monitoring systems collect waveforms and spectra for diagnostics: orbit shapes, bearing defect frequencies, imbalance, misalignment, looseness. Trending turns failing components into planned work, and API 670 defines the standard hardware architecture for critical trains.

process_steps.name: Proximity, velocity and acceleration sensors measure machine motion
Monitoring system computes amplitudes, alarms and trips
Spectra, orbits and trends diagnosed for fault signatures
Findings route to planned maintenance or operational limits

name: Propane-precooled mixed refrigerant liquefaction (C3MR, AP-X)
principle: A propane refrigeration cycle precools the feed gas and the mixed refrigerant. A mixed refrigerant of nitrogen, methane, ethane and propane then liquefies and subcools the gas in a coil-wound main cryogenic heat exchanger. AP-X adds a nitrogen expander loop that subcools LNG from about -115 °C to about -150 °C, cutting mixed refrigerant flow by 40% per unit of LNG and allowing trains of 7.8 Mtpa and more.

name: Dual mixed refrigerant liquefaction
principle: Two mixed refrigerant cycles replace the propane-plus-mixed-refrigerant arrangement. name: Floating storage and regasification units (FSRU)

name: Corrosion under insulation (CUI)
principle: Water ingress into insulation creates an invisible electrolyte film against hot or cold steel, producing the most widespread hidden-corrosion mechanism on process plants: pitting and general loss under cladding that looks intact from outside. Management combines risk ranking (temperature band, insulation type, coating age, environment), inspection through insulation with pulsed eddy current where possible and targeted stripping where not, and prevention at the source: high-quality CUI-resistant coatings applied before insulation, sealed cladding, and design that avoids water traps.

Screened through insulation with pulsed eddy current; hot spots flagged
Targeted insulation stripping and visual/UT confirmation at flagged points
Prevention: CUI coatings, cladding sealed, water traps designed out

name: Acetic acid (methanol carbonylation)
principle: Methanol reacts with carbon monoxide in the presence of an iodide promoter and a rhodium (Monsanto) or iridium (Cativa) catalyst. Iridium lets the reaction run with less water, which needs fewer drying columns, gives fewer by-products such as propionic acid and suppresses the water-gas shift. The two processes can share the same plant.
advantages: Less water and fewer by-products than rhodium (Wikipedia)
limitations: Source gives no yields or conditions

name: Electric steam cracking
applications: low-carbon ethylene and propylene when power is renewable
principle: The gas-fired radiant coils of a steam cracker are replaced by coils heated with electricity, so the furnace itself emits no combustion CO2. The rest of the plant (quench, compression, cryogenic separation) is unchanged, which makes the route a retrofit option for existing crackers if renewable power and grid capacity are available.

name: Methanol-to-olefins (MTO, DMTO)
applications: ethylene and propylene from coal- or gas-derived methanol
polyethylene and polypropylene in coal-rich regions
principle: Methanol vapour is converted over a SAPO-34 molecular sieve catalyst in a fluidized-bed reactor into ethylene and propylene. The catalyst coke is burned off in a regenerator, and the product gas is quenched, compressed and separated. DMTO-II adds a second reactor that cracks C4 and heavier by-products over a dual-function catalyst to raise olefin yield; DMTO-III raises selectivity further without recycling C4+.

name: Paraxylene adsorption and crystallisation
applications: paraxylene for purified terephthalic acid and polyester
principle: Mixed xylenes from reformate and transalkylation are fed to a simulated-moving-bed adsorption unit. A rotary valve moves feed, desorbent and product ports along beds of selective adsorbent so that, in effect, a counter-current moving bed is created without moving solids; paraxylene is adsorbed and then desorbed, and the desorbent is recovered by distillation. The raffinate is isomerised and recycled to extinction.

name: Plastics pyrolysis (chemical recycling)

principle: Mixed post-consumer plastic waste, mainly polyolefins, is heated without oxygen so that the polymers crack into a hydrocarbon oil (called TACOIL by Plastic Energy), gas and char. name: Polyethylene (gas phase, slurry, solution)
principle: Ethylene, with a comonomer such as butene or hexene for LLDPE and HDPE copolymers, is polymerised on a supported catalyst in a gas-phase fluidized-bed, slurry-loop or solution reactor. The process route and catalyst (Ziegler-Natta, chromium or metallocene) set the grade range.

name: Catalyst management (handling, regeneration, recycling)
principle: Catalyst is a consumable with a managed life: fresh catalyst is loaded under inert atmosphere with density and distribution control; activity declines through coking, poisoning and sintering and is watched via bed pressure drop and product quality; spent catalyst is unloaded (often under inert, sometimes offline via skimming), then either regenerated in-situ or sent to a specialist reclaimer that recovers metals and reconditions the carrier. Life-cycle contracts bundle supply, loading, surveillance and disposal so the refiner pays for active-days rather than tonnes.

name: Gas-fired steam and hot-water boilers
applications: process steam for refineries, petrochemical and industrial plants

fuel-flexible CFB steam generation and solid-fuel-to-gas conversion
principle: A gas-fired boiler burns natural gas (or another gaseous fuel) in a contained furnace and transfers the heat through pressure-part surfaces to water, producing steam or hot water. Package fire-tube boilers pass hot gas through tubes surrounded by water; water-tube boilers pass water through tubes in the gas path and separate steam in a drum or use once-through circuits; condensing designs cool the flue gas below its dew point to recover latent heat. Low-NOx burners, flue-gas recirculation and post-combustion catalysts control emissions. Heat recovery steam generators raise steam from gas-turbine exhaust and may burn additional gas in the duct.

process_steps.name: Gas and combustion air are metered and conditioned
equipment: double block and bleed shutoff valves

process_steps.name: Low-NOx burner fires into the water-cooled furnace
Heat crosses the heat-transfer surfaces into boiler water
Steam separates and is conditioned for export or the turbine
Condensate and make-up are deaerated, heated and pumped back
Flue gas passes heat recovery and emission controls to the stack

key_equipment: burner management and flame safeguard system
fire tubes or water tubes and tube sheets
safety relief valves and blowdown system

name: Microreactors (transportable nuclear)
principle: Very small nuclear reactors, roughly 1 to 75 MWe, that are fabricated and fuelled in a factory, shipped complete in standard containers and installed on a small site, running for years without on-site refuelling. Designs use heat pipes (Westinghouse eVinci, 5 MWe), high-temperature gas cooling with TRISO fuel (BWXT BANR, 75 MWt) or liquid-metal fast cooling on HALEU (Oklo Aurora, up to 75 MWe). No commercial unit operates yet: the eVinci test reactor reached criticality in September 2026, and Oklo targets commercial operation at Idaho National Laboratory in 2028.

notes: The eVinci test reactor is a scaled-down 3 MWt unit at the NRIC DOME test bed in Idaho (DOE approved its preliminary safety design report in June 2025, the first for a microreactor developer). Oklo's INL unit is being built under DOE authorisation, to be converted to an NRC commercial licence. The US Army selected eVinci for the next phase of its Janus programme in August 2026 (energy.gov article read 26 October 2026). Process provenance: the deployment sequence is as Westinghouse described it to the NRC - factory assembly with fuel loaded there, transport to site, installation and operation, then refuelling/refurbishment or decommissioning with the irradiated reactor transported away; a 5 MWe unit on under 3 acres with a 0.4-acre reactor building and 200 sq ft basemat, shipped as packaged modules. name: Modular reciprocating engine power plants
principle: Power plants built from factory-fabricated modules: an engine, generator and auxiliaries are assembled and tested in a factory enclosure (a genset container or a multi-megawatt power block), shipped complete and bolted together on a prepared foundation, with no site welding. Wärtsilä's Modular Block takes one 34SG generating set per block, Rolls-Royce (mtu) offers factory-tested 10, 20 and 30 MW power blocks for plants of five to several hundred megawatts, and Everllence (formerly MAN Energy Solutions) modularises engine-specific systems for its 51/60 series plants.

name: Modular ORC units for waste heat and small geothermal
applications: reciprocating engine and turbine exhaust heat
principle: Organic Rankine Cycle modules in the tens of kW to multi-MW range convert heat sources from about 70 to 400 degrees C into electricity using a low-boiling working fluid in a skid- or container-mounted unit. name: Powerships and power barges
applications: fast capacity addition for national grids
principle: A complete engine or gas-turbine power plant is installed on a ship hull or barge, moored at a port or prepared basin and connected to the onshore grid through a switchyard, so a country adds 30 to 470 MW of capacity in weeks without land acquisition or construction. name: Delayed coking and fluid coking
applications: petroleum coke for fuel or anodes
principle: Vacuum residue is heated quickly in a furnace to 480 to 590 °C and sent to a coke drum at about 400 °C and 25 to 30 psig, where it cracks thermally over many hours. Vapours go to a fractionator, and solid coke builds up in the drum. Drums run in pairs on a semi-batch cycle of 28 to 36 hours, with one filling while the other is steamed, cooled and cut out with high-pressure water.

performance.basis: EPA AP-42 description

source.note: US EPA AP-42 Section 5.1 Petroleum Refining (April 2015 revision), process descriptions

performance.basis: EPA AP-42 description, start of feed to start of next feed to the same drum

source.note: US EPA AP-42 Section 5.1 Petroleum Refining (April 2015 revision), process descriptions

advantages: Robust destruction of the heaviest residues
Lower pressure and hydrogen demand than resid hydrocracking
limitations: Produces large volumes of coke
Cracked products need severe hydrotreating
Drum cycling and decoking are safety-critical

name: Direct crude cracking
principle: Crude oil, or a light fraction of it, is sent directly to a steam cracker to make olefins and aromatics, skipping some or all of the conventional distillation and conversion steps. ExxonMobil's Singapore cracker started up in 2013 as the first to process crude directly. Saudi Aramco, Lummus and Chevron Lummus Global developed TC2C, which uses steam dilution to vaporise a light cut for the cracker, hydroprocesses a heart cut, and converts the heaviest fraction in liquid-circulation reactors.

name: Fluid catalytic cracking and resid FCC
principle: Hot, fine zeolite catalyst behaves like a fluid and meets vaporised gas oil in a riser reactor at 470 to 525 °C, cracking it into gasoline, LPG, light cycle oil and slurry. Coke deposited on the catalyst is burned off with air in a regenerator at 590 to 675 °C, which reheats the catalyst for the next pass. Residue versions use two-stage regenerators and catalyst coolers.

name: Flare gas recovery and smokeless flares
principle: Elevated flares burn relief and vent gas at the tip of a stack 10 to over 100 m tall, using steam or air assistance for smokeless burning; ground flares burn at ground level, often in enclosures. EPA's AP-42 says properly operated flares achieve at least 98% destruction efficiency, with refinery flares needing at least 270 Btu/ft3 net heating value in the combustion zone. Flare gas recovery compressors return routine flow to fuel gas; see the upstream flare gas recovery card.

name: Visbreaking and solvent deasphalting
principle: Visbreaking mildly thermally cracks vacuum residue to cut its viscosity so less cutter stock is needed for fuel oil. Solvent deasphalting extracts deasphalted oil (DAO) from residue with a light hydrocarbon solvent, leaving asphaltenes or pitch; KBR's ROSE uses supercritical solvent recovery. DAO feeds FCC, hydrocrackers or lube plants.

name: Chemical EOR (polymer and surfactant flooding)
applications: extra oil from mature waterflooded fields
principle: Chemicals are added to injection water to recover oil that waterflooding leaves behind. Polymers such as hydrolyzed polyacrylamide (HPAM) raise the viscosity of the injected water so it sweeps the reservoir more evenly and water breaks through later. Surfactants lower the interfacial tension between oil and water so trapped oil droplets can move. Alkali-surfactant-polymer (ASP) combines both. Polymer and surfactant performance depends on salinity, temperature, adsorption on the rock and injectivity, so candidates are screened in the laboratory and by core flooding before a field pilot.

name: CO2 enhanced oil recovery (miscible CO2 flooding)
applications: storage of captured CO2 in oil fields
principle: CO2 is compressed and injected into an oil reservoir, usually one already waterflooded, where at or above the minimum miscibility pressure it mixes with the crude, swells it and lowers its viscosity so that residual oil can be swept to producing wells. Water and CO2 are often injected in alternating slugs (WAG). Produced CO2 is separated from oil and water, recompressed and reinjected, so most purchased CO2 stays underground.

name: Well plug and abandonment (cement plugs, rig-based)
applications: permanent closure of wells at end of life
decommissioning of platforms and subsea wells
principle: A well that is no longer needed is permanently sealed so that formation fluids cannot reach the surface. Barriers, usually cement plugs set across producing zones, above the liner top and near the surface, are placed from a rig after the well is killed and equipment is removed. Standards differ in the barriers they require, for example Indonesia's SNI 13-6910-2002 and Norway's NORSOK D-010, and the choice drives cost. Newer methods such as through-tubing abandonment aim to avoid pulling the completion.

name: Aerobic granular sludge treatment (Nereda)
applications: municipal wastewater with simultaneous N and P removal
retrofits that need capacity without new tanks
principle: Follows the Royal HaskoningDHV Nereda licensor flow: one cyclical SBR-style reactor with a granular biomass that settles 3-8x faster than flocculent sludge. Simultaneous nitrification/denitrification and bio-P removal happen inside the dense granules (aerobic shell, anoxic/anaerobic core). The published Nereda cycle is: (1) feed/draw from the bottom while decanted clear water leaves the top, (2) aeration/reaction with simultaneous fill, (3) settling of the fast-settling granules, (4) decant of treated effluent; excess sludge is wasted as well-settling granules that dewater easily.

name: Internal-circulation anaerobic reactor (Paques BIOPAQ IC)
applications: high-strength industrial effluent (breweries, sugar, pulp & paper, food)
COD removal with on-site biogas production
principle: Follows the Paques BIOPAQ IC licensor flow: a tall (16-28 m) reactor treats wastewater in two stages inside one vessel. In the first stage the upflow anaerobic sludge blanket converts most COD to biogas; the gas is captured in the first separator and the rising gas-lift drives an internal circulation loop that returns the mixed liquor to the reactor bottom without external pumps. The pre-treated water then flows to a second, low-loading polishing stage with a gas separator at the top. The published Paques arrangement is: influent distribution at the bottom, first-stage granular sludge blanket, gas-liquid separator and gas-lift riser/downer forming the internal circulation, second polishing stage, treated-water outlet with optional degassing.

name: Membrane bioreactor (MBR) wastewater treatment
applications: water recycling for irrigation and industry
principle: A membrane bioreactor replaces the secondary clarifier of an activated-sludge plant with a submerged ultrafiltration/microfiltration membrane unit inside (or immediately after) the bioreactor. Mixed liquor is filtered directly at 0.1-0.4 um, giving a solids-free, turbidity-low effluent ready for disinfection or RO reuse, at a much smaller footprint and higher mixed-liquor concentration (8-15 g/L MLSS typical). Per licensor-first rule this card follows the Kubota Submerged Membrane Unit (SMU) flat-plate configuration published by Kubota Water & Environment: coarse screening to fine screening, equalisation, anoxic/aerobic bioreactor, submerged flat-plate membrane tank with coarse-bubble air scour, permeate drawn at low trans-membrane pressure, and in-tank membrane cleaning by backwash with chlorine and periodic recovery chemical clean.

name: Spent caustic treatment (wet air oxidation)
principle: Spent caustic from mercaptan removal, ethylene quench and refinery LPG treating carries sulfides, mercaptides, cresylates and naphthenates at high pH. Wet air oxidation (WAO) oxidises these with air at elevated temperature and pressure so the effluent is biologically treatable; IPIECA notes spent caustic should be neutralised or routed to equalisation to protect the API separators. Linde has supplied WAO since 1970; Evoqua carries the Zimpro legacy.

principle: Follows the Paques BIOPAQ UASB licensor flow: wastewater is fed evenly at the bottom of a tall reactor and flows upward through a dense blanket of anaerobic granular sludge that converts COD to biogas; a three-phase (gas-liquid-solid) separator at the top retains granules, degasses the effluent and discharges treated water. name: Water minimisation and reuse pinch for industry
principle: Mass-exchange pinch analysis treats water as a network resource: each use has a limiting contaminant concentration, so streams can be cascaded from the cleanest duty to the dirtiest before treatment. Targeting gives the minimum fresh-water and wastewater flows, and a regenerator (DAF, membrane, ion exchange) placed at the pinch relaxes the constraint, cutting both intake and downstream ZLD load.

name: Zero liquid discharge (ZLD)
applications: coal-power and refinery effluent with no outfall
principle: Licensor-first (Aquatech published trains): pretreated wastewater passes membrane concentration (RO/HERO), then mechanical vapour-recompression or falling-film evaporators, then spray-dryers or forced-circulation crystallisers; distillate is recycled to process and salts crystallise as a solid product/waste — no liquid discharge. Aquatech published performance: brine concentrated to >250,000 mg/L TDS; distillate <10 mg/L.
